# Prikk installer (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7).
#
# Generated by `prikk-release-policy generate-installer` at release time and published as a
# release asset (never committed as a tracked .ps1 file) -- see docs/src/guide/install.md.
#
# A passing checksum here proves this download matches what the release page published; it does
# not prove *who* published it. In v0 one maintainer key signs every release tag; release-signers.toml
# is empty because no multi-signer policy exists yet -- see the release, versioning, and compatibility
# reference for the full statement. This script never claims more than that.
#
# Usage (the one-line form; code piped to Invoke-Expression is not subject to execution policy,
# unlike a saved .ps1 file run directly -- see docs/src/guide/install.md for the downloaded-file
# form and what to do about execution policy there):
#   irm https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
#
# Environment overrides (there are no --version/--prefix flags here, unlike install.sh: the
# one-line `irm | iex` form has no way to forward positional arguments the way `sh -s --
# --version X.Y.Z` does, so environment variables are the only override this script supports):
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_VERSION   version tag to install, default "latest"
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR       install directory, default "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\prikk"
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_BASE_URL  override the download base URL (undocumented, test-only)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# Windows PowerShell 5.1's default TLS negotiation can fall short of the TLS 1.2 GitHub's release
# CDN requires, depending on the machine's own .NET/OS defaults -- this is a documented Windows
# PowerShell 5.1 gotcha (Microsoft's TLS 1.2 guidance for older .NET Framework defaults), not
# something this script measured on a real 5.1 runtime (none is available in this project's own
# development environment -- see the report). PowerShell 7 (.NET) already defaults to TLS 1.2+ and
# tolerates this call as a harmless compatibility shim, so it is set unconditionally rather than
# conditioned on $PSVersionTable.
try {
  [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol -bor [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
} catch {
  # Best effort only; if the type or value does not exist on this runtime, downloading below will
  # fail with its own clear error instead.
}

$repo = "REPO_SLUG"
$version = if ($env:PRIKK_INSTALL_VERSION) { $env:PRIKK_INSTALL_VERSION } else { "latest" }
$installDir = if ($env:PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR) { $env:PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR } else { Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\prikk" }

# `[System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture` is preferred over the
# $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE environment variable, which a WOW64 (32-bit-on-64-bit) process can
# see rewritten for the process's own architecture rather than the OS's -- confirmed from .NET's
# own documentation, not measured here. It requires .NET Framework 4.7.1+, present on every
# Windows 10/11 install this project supports; the catch below falls back to the environment
# variable if it is somehow unavailable, rather than refusing outright.
try {
  $isX64 = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture -eq [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Architecture]::X64
} catch {
  $isX64 = $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE -eq "AMD64"
}

if (-not $isX64) {
  Write-Error "prikk-install: no prebuilt binary for Windows/$([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture) (only x86_64 ships one)"
  Write-Host "prikk-install: download prikk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from the release page by hand," -ForegroundColor Yellow
  Write-Host "prikk-install: or run 'cargo install prikk'" -ForegroundColor Yellow
  exit 1
}
$target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"

if ($env:PRIKK_INSTALL_BASE_URL) {
  # Undocumented for ordinary use; exists so this script's own download-verify-extract logic can
  # be tested against a fixture server instead of the real release page -- the same purpose
  # install.sh's identical override serves.
  $baseUrl = $env:PRIKK_INSTALL_BASE_URL
} elseif ($version -eq "latest") {
  $baseUrl = "https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download"
} else {
  $baseUrl = "https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$version"
}

$asset = "prikk-$target.zip"
$workDir = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("prikk-install-" + [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName())
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $workDir | Out-Null

try {
  $assetPath = Join-Path $workDir $asset
  $checksumPath = Join-Path $workDir "$asset.sha256"

  Write-Host "prikk-install: downloading $asset ($version, $target)"
  # -UseBasicParsing: Windows PowerShell 5.1 otherwise tries to parse the response through the IE
  # engine, which can fail on a machine where Internet Explorer's first-run configuration was never
  # completed -- a documented 5.1 gotcha. PowerShell 7 accepts the same flag as a no-op.
  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$baseUrl/$asset" -OutFile $assetPath -UseBasicParsing
  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$baseUrl/$asset.sha256" -OutFile $checksumPath -UseBasicParsing

  Write-Host "prikk-install: verifying checksum"
  # The .sha256 line shape was matched to sha256sum's own output on purpose (RFC 107 Stage 2):
  # lowercase hex, two spaces, no trailing newline -- so the comparison below is a plain string
  # compare of the hex, lowercased on both sides since Get-FileHash returns uppercase by default.
  $expectedLine = (Get-Content -Path $checksumPath -Raw).Trim()
  $expectedHash = ($expectedLine -split '\s+')[0].ToLowerInvariant()
  $actualHash = (Get-FileHash -Path $assetPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
  if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) {
    Write-Error "prikk-install: checksum verification failed; refusing to install"
    exit 1
  }

  Write-Host "prikk-install: extracting"
  Expand-Archive -Path $assetPath -DestinationPath $workDir -Force

  $extractedExe = Join-Path $workDir "prikk.exe"
  if (-not (Test-Path -Path $extractedExe -PathType Leaf)) {
    Write-Error "prikk-install: extracted archive did not contain a prikk.exe binary"
    exit 1
  }

  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $installDir | Out-Null
  # Overwrites unconditionally, the same as install.sh's own `mv` over any existing binary at the
  # install path -- neither script checks for or prompts about an existing install first.
  Copy-Item -Path $extractedExe -Destination (Join-Path $installDir "prikk.exe") -Force

  Write-Host "prikk-install: installed to $installDir\prikk.exe"

  $markerPath = Join-Path $installDir "path-added-by-install.marker"
  $userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User')
  $pathEntries = @()
  if ($userPath) {
    $pathEntries = $userPath -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' }
  }
  $alreadyOnPath = $pathEntries -contains $installDir

  if (-not $alreadyOnPath) {
    # User Path only, never the machine's -- [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(..., 'Machine')
    # requires administrator rights and would affect every account on the machine; install.sh has
    # no such distinction to mirror since a shell rc file is already per-user.
    $newPath = if ($userPath) { "$userPath;$installDir" } else { $installDir }
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', $newPath, 'User')
    # install.sh does not prompt before appending to a shell rc file; this script follows the same
    # rule and does not prompt before this PATH change either -- see the report for the open
    # question of whether both should.
    Set-Content -Path $markerPath -Value "This file records that install.ps1 added $installDir to this user's PATH.`r`nuninstall.ps1 reads it to decide whether to remove that PATH entry.`r`nDelete it only if you understand why." -NoNewline
    Write-Host "prikk-install: added $installDir to your user PATH (open a new terminal for it to take effect)"
  } else {
    Write-Host "prikk-install: $installDir is already on your user PATH"
  }

  Write-Host "prikk-install: done. Run 'prikk --version' (in a new terminal, if PATH was just updated)."
  Write-Host "prikk-install: this checksum proves the download matches what the release page published;"
  Write-Host "prikk-install: it does not prove who published it. In v0 one maintainer key signs every release"
  Write-Host "prikk-install: tag; release-signers.toml is empty because no multi-signer policy exists yet."
} finally {
  Remove-Item -Path $workDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
